Curr no. 98 is already in our bibliography, read and silent on accent (and headed Kulkadoon…

sources.note: nothing; the database holds no kinship terminology or vocabulary for Wakabunga, only the four section names in three secondary sources (all traceable to Roth 1897's Table I), which confirms independently of AUSTLANG that no lexical material exists on which an accent statement could rest

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. 1990. Languages of the Queensland/Northern Territory border: updating the classification. In Peter Austin, R.M.W. Dixon, Tom Dutton & Isobel White (eds), Language and history: Essays in honour of Luise A. Hercus (Pacific Linguistics C-116), 49-65. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 52: 'There is no information available on Wakabunga. On the basis of its location, and the fact that there is an unnamed vocabulary (Curr 1886 vol.2: 318) that comes from this location and which is a Mayi dialect, I suspect that Wakabunga is a Mayi dialect.'

sources.note: no phonology content; ethnographic catalogue entry whose only reference is Roth 1897 - establishes that Roth is the sole primary source behind the Tindale/AUSTLANG/ISO chain

sources.citation: Roth, Walter E. 1910. North Queensland Ethnography. Bulletin No. 18. Social and individual nomenclature. Records of the Australian Museum 8(1): 79-106, pls. xxv-xxxi. doi:10.3853/j.0067-1975.8.1910.936.
sources.note: Nothing. Checked because Roth is the only first-hand recorder of the 'Workoboongo' and this bulletin is his final statement on Queensland group names: the name does not occur anywhere in the 43-page text (Acrobat text; a full-text search for stress/accent every variant plus a census of all W- tokens), the north-western districts are explicitly left to Roth 1897 (p. 84), and the Leichhardt-Selwyn Ranges row of the section/totem table (p. 103) is labelled Kalkadun. Closes the 'later Roth bulletins' route; adds no data.

sources.citation: Roth, Walter E. 1897. Ethnological studies among the north-west-central Queensland Aborigines. Brisbane: Edmund Gregory, Government Printer; London: Queensland Agent-General. xvi+199 pp., 24 pls. (ch. I sect. 3 orthography, pp. 1-2; sect. 46 p. 41; ch. III sect. 62 Table I, p. 57).
sources.note: No statement about Wakabunga accent. The only first-hand Wakabunga (Workoboongo) words ever printed are these four section names, each with its accented syllable italicised under Roth's convention: initial in Pa-ting-o, Ka-poo-dung-o, Mar-ing-o; third syllable in the four-syllable Jim-mi-ling-o (the same name is accented the same way in the Miubbi column). This is wordlist-only accent marking on 4 items (3 of 4 initial), not a description; the names are shared regional section terms (cf. Kalkadoon Pa-ting-o, Miubbi Jim-mi-ling-o, Mar-ing-o) and may not even be native Wakabunga vocabulary.

sources.citation: Urquhart, F. & Joseph O'Reilley. 1886. No. 98. Seymour, Templeton, and Cloncurry Rivers. In E. M. Curr (ed.), The Australian race, vol. II, 326-329. Melbourne: John Ferres, Government Printer.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Curr labels it a Kulkadoon (Kalkatungu) vocabulary; 'Waukaboonia' appears only as the name of a neighbouring tribe (p. 327). Wikipedia notes some attach this list to Wakabunga; the text itself does not.
